title: Uncontracted log tower pullbacks and normalized contraction comparisons
statement:
For a log morphism $f:Y\to X$ of locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] and finite saturated log blowup towers $A$ over $X$ and $B$ over $Y$ [def-trf-strict-etale-log-blowup-procedure], a full (uncontracted) recursive pullback consists of order isomorphisms between all their levels and stages, preserving initial, before, and after indices, log maps $B_i\to A_i$ starting at $f$, fs Cartesian squares at each arrow [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup], and equality of the actual centers with generated pullback ideals. No stage is deleted. The projection of each level to its base is the composite of its arrows [def-per-strict-log-blowup-procedure]. A tower is contracted if none of its centers is the whole log monoid sheaf. A full pullback is cover-synchronized if every level square over its base is a scheme-theoretic pullback, every level map is surjective strict etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and a center is whole exactly when its pulled-back center is whole.

For contractions $c:D\rightsquigarrow C$ and $d:E\rightsquigarrow F$, a full pullback $p:E\to D$ over $v:W\to Y$, and a full pullback $q:U\to C$ over $v$, an interchange isomorphism $e:U\simeq F$ is normalized when its count and retained-stage maps identify exactly the same original labels and its level composites satisfy $c_iq_{c(i)}e_{q(c(i))}=p_i d_{p(i)}$, including the log-section maps. Restriction of an ordered tower isomorphism means commutativity with the full-pullback projections, with the corresponding level and stage indices. An isomorphism $C\simeq A$ induces a local isomorphism $F\simeq v^*A$ if its full pullback is that local isomorphism composed with the interchange, including actual log morphisms and ordered indices. A comparison restricts along a full pullback when its count and retained-stage maps are transported by the full ordered identifications and its log maps are composed with the full-pullback maps. The identity comparison has identity count and retained embeddings and identity log maps; its restriction agrees with the full pullback. A composite comparison has the composite count maps and retained embeddings and the composite log morphisms [lem-sfb-log-morphism-operations]. These are predicates on the prescribed data, not choices of objects or arbitrary maps.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.11 and proof of 3.3.15, printed pp.107--110 (PDF pp.113--116): full recursive pullback, contraction, and comparison by descent.
